Topics · Death and what comes after

Must I purify myself, or can another do it?

Like the Buddha, the Quran says no one bears another's load and effort lasts. Purity itself comes with grace.

Part 1 of 4

﴿وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۚ وَإِن تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ إِلَىٰ حِمْلِهَا لَا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَىْءٌ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰٓ ۗ إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَأَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ ۚ وَمَن تَزَكَّىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمَصِيرُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to [carry some of] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a close relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and have established prayer. And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for [the benefit of] his soul. And to Allāh is the [final] destination.

Quran · Fatir 35:18

Translation

The soul who sins, he shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be on him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be on him.

Original · Hebrew

הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא־יִשָּׂ֣א ׀ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב וְאָב֙ לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הַבֵּ֔ן צִדְקַ֤ת הַצַּדִּיק֙ עָלָ֣יו תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְרִשְׁעַ֥ת הָרָשָׁ֖ע עָלָ֥יו תִּֽהְיֶֽה׃

Ezekiel · 18:20

World English Bible

The Dhammapada has the Buddha say that no one purifies another. This verse says two things beside it: no soul carries the burden of another, and whoever purifies himself does so for his own soul. Even if a heavily loaded soul calls a relative to carry some of it, nothing is carried. It may sound heavy at first, but it is generous too: it says purification is real, and within reach of every soul.

A question for you

Which is closer to your experience: others made you better, or you did the work?

If you sayOthers helped, and the work was mine
ThenThat is what the verse and the Buddha's line agree on: help is present, and the final work cannot be carried for anyone.
If you sayI did it alone
ThenThat may be true in one aspect. The verse says purifying is for your own soul, and a later verse here adds something about grace.
If you sayI have not yet
ThenThe verse says it is within your reach. It does not tell you to begin; it says the door is open.

Part 2 of 4

﴿أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ٣٨ وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَـٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ٣٩ وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُۥ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ٤٠ ثُمَّ يُجْزَىٰهُ ٱلْجَزَآءَ ٱلْأَوْفَىٰ٤١﴾

Translation of the meaning

That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives And that his effort is going to be seen - Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense -

Quran · An-Najm 53:38-41

Translation

Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.

Original · Hebrew

וּלְךָֽ־אֲדֹנָ֥י חָ֑סֶד כִּֽי־אַתָּ֨ה תְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּֽמַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

the Psalms · 62:12

World English Bible

Three short statements: no soul carries another's load. A person has only what he strove for. And his striving will be seen. The third is the quiet comfort in the verse: effort is neither lost nor hidden. This is close to the Buddha's teaching that each person must strive, and that teachers only point to the road. Then comes the recompense, in full, with nothing taken from it.

A question for you

Which of these three lines gives you the most hope?

If you sayNo one carries another's load
ThenThere is a hidden relief in it: no one carries what you did, and you do not carry what another did. The soul is freed from a weight it never made.
If you sayA person has what he strove for
ThenThat means your effort is yours, and no one takes it. It is very close to the Buddha's saying that the effort is the person's.
If you sayThe striving will be seen
ThenA true word of hope: that unseen effort is not wasted.

Part 3 of 4

﴿فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُذَكِّرٌ٢١ لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُصَيْطِرٍ٢٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

So remind, [O Muḥammad]; you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller.

Quran · Al-Ghashiyah 88:21-22

You yourself must make an effort. The Tathagatas (Buddhas) are only preachers. The thoughtful who enter the way are freed from the bondage of Mara.

Buddhist texts · Dhp 276

Max Müller, 1881

If no one purifies another, what does a teacher do? The Dhammapada has the Buddha say: the effort is yours to make; the teachers only point to the road. The Quran says to its Messenger: you are only one who reminds; you are not set over them as a controller. A teacher reminds and shows the way, and does not compel. The two texts resemble each other in how far they say a teacher can reach. This leaves the choice with the reader.

A question for you

What is the difference between one who shows you the road and one who walks it in your place?

If you sayThe first leaves me free
ThenThat freedom is what the verse protects: not set over them as a controller. The freedom here is not a gap; it is the point.
If you sayThe second cannot exist
ThenThat is close to the first verse here: no one carries for another. There is no one who can walk in your place, even if he wished.
If you sayThe difference is only in the tiredness
ThenPerhaps. The verse keeps the deeper sense: that arriving is yours, whatever the help.

Part 4 of 4

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ ۚ وَمَن يَتَّبِعْ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ ۚ وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًا وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُزَكِّى مَن يَشَآءُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan - indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing. And if not for the favor of Allāh upon you and His mercy, not one of you would have been pure, ever, but Allāh purifies whom He wills, and Allāh is Hearing and Knowing.

Quran · An-Nur 24:21

Translation

Therefore, putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor, for we are members of one another. “Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath, and don’t give place to the devil.

Original · Ancient Greek

Διὸ ἀποθέμενοι τὸ ψεῦδος λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐσμὲν ἀλλήλων μέλη. ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε· ὁ ἥλιος μὴ ἐπιδυέτω ἐπὶ παροργισμῷ ὑμῶν, μηδὲ δίδοτε τόπον τῷ διαβόλῳ.

Ephesians · 4:25-27

World English Bible

Here the Quran adds one thing more. The verse says no one would ever be pure but for God's grace and mercy, and that it is God who purifies whom He wills. So it agrees that no human being purifies another, and adds that purity does not come without grace. Your effort is real and God's grace is real, and the verse holds both. This does not cancel effort; it is a hope above it.

A question for you

Where do effort and grace meet in what you know of your own tradition?

If you sayEffort alone is the path
ThenA common reading among many. The Quran fully acknowledges effort, then adds grace, not in its place but beside it.
If you sayAnother power helps, like a vow or a grace
ThenThat is the reading of certain Buddhist schools, Pure Land among them. It meets what the verse says here.
If you sayI have not thought about this before
ThenThen it is a good question to sit with. The closing step asks you to say what you carry from it now.

The same in the other books

who “will pay back to everyone according to their works:”

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ ἔδωκεν ἡ θάλασσα τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἔδωκαν τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐκρίθησαν ἕκαστος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν.

but the children of the murderers he didn’t put to death, according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, as Yahweh commanded, saying, “The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children be put to death for the fathers; but every man shall die for his own sin.”

וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י הַמַּכִּ֖ים לֹ֣א הֵמִ֑ית כַּכָּת֣וּב בְּסֵ֣פֶר תּֽוֹרַת־מֹ֠שֶׁה אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹא־יוּמְת֨וּ אָב֤וֹת עַל־בָּנִים֙ וּבָנִים֙ לֹא־יוּמְת֣וּ עַל־אָב֔וֹת כִּ֛י אִם־אִ֥ישׁ בְּחֶטְא֖וֹ יוּמָֽת׃
